verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.180
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 4.180

verses.pali: 18. Sañcetaniyavagga
verses.english: 18. Intention

verses.pali: Mahāpadesasutta
verses.english: The Four Great References

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bhoganagare viharati ānandacetiye.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near the Bhoga City, at the Ānanda Shrine.

verses.pali: Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,

verses.pali: “bhikkhavo”ti.
verses.english: “Mendicants!”

verses.pali: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Venerable sir,” they replied.

verses.pali: Bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “cattārome, bhikkhave, mahāpadese desessāmi,
verses.english: “Mendicants, I will teach you the four great references.

verses.pali: taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
verses.english: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Yes, sir,” they replied.

verses.pali: Bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “Katame, bhikkhave, cattāro mahāpadesā?
verses.english: “Mendicants, what are the four great references?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
verses.english: Take a mendicant who says:

verses.pali: ‘sammukhā metaṁ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ—
verses.english: ‘Reverend, I have heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

verses.pali: ayaṁ dhammo, ayaṁ vinayo, idaṁ satthusāsanan’ti.
verses.english: this is the teaching, this is the training, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

verses.pali: Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṁ neva abhinanditabbaṁ nappaṭikkositabbaṁ.
verses.english: You should neither approve nor reject that mendicant’s statement.

verses.pali: Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṁ uggahetvā sutte otāretabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni.
verses.english: Instead, having carefully memorized those words and phrases, you should make sure they fit in the discourse and are exhibited in the training.

verses.pali: Tāni ce sutte otāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte otaranti na vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṁ:
verses.english: If they do not fit in the discourse and are not exhibited in the training, you should draw the conclusion:

verses.pali: ‘addhā idaṁ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassa;
verses.english: ‘Clearly this is not the word of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

verses.pali: imassa ca bhikkhuno duggahitan’ti.
verses.english: It has been incorrectly memorized by that mendicant.’

verses.pali: Iti hetaṁ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha.
verses.english: And so you should discard it.

verses.pali: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
verses.english: Take another mendicant who says:

verses.pali: ‘sammukhā metaṁ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ—
verses.english: ‘Reverend, I have heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

verses.pali: Dasamaṁ.
Sañcetaniyavaggo tatiyo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Cetanā vibhatti koṭṭhiko,
Ānando upavāṇapañcamaṁ;
Āyācana rāhula jambālī,
Nibbānaṁ mahāpadesenāti.
